subject.title: [Security] Input validation bypass in approval-classifier configuration loading

question: Does the reporter's malformed object reach ACP approval classification from an untrusted input and cause a tool to receive a less restrictive approval class?
rationale: The public report does not identify the data origin or resulting behavior, and OpenClaw treats operator-controlled configuration differently from untrusted protocol or model input; that trust-boundary determination must precede a fix.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Route the reporter to a private GitHub Security Advisory and require an exact payload, current SHA, call path, classification delta, and demonstrated impact before scoping code changes.

options.title: Treat as config hardening
options.body: If only a trusted operator can write the object and no approval boundary is crossed, track any useful type validation as ordinary defense-in-depth rather than a vulnerability.

options.title: Close after source confirmation
options.body: Close as unsupported if maintainers confirm there is no approval-classifier configuration loading path matching the report and the reporter cannot provide a reproduction.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Route the reporter to a private GitHub Security Advisory and require an exact payload, current SHA, call path, classification delta, and demonstrated impact before scoping code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects this contributor most directly to the semantic ACP approval-classification boundary described by the report.
